texts.preamble: Anand Vikram Singh Bhadoriya vs Virendra Kumar Jain on 6 July, 2017 Crr-2642-2015 (Anand Vikram Singh Bhadoriya Vs Virendra Kumar Jain) 06-07-2017 Shri Ramesh Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners. Shri Aman Chouraisa, learned counsel for respondent No.1. This revision under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C. has been directed against order dated 17/03/2015 passed by Second Asj, Sagar in Criminal Revision No.81/2015, setting aside order dated 19/02/2015 passed by learned Jmfc, Sagar in criminal Case No.2192/2014. Brief facts just necessary for disposal of this petition are that the respondent No.1 is the shopkeeper. The Food Inspector has bought the pouch of Pan Masala from the shop of respondent No.1 when the sample was sent for analysis to the Food Testing Laboratory, Bhopal it was found to be unsafe for human consumption as 3.408% Magnesium Carbonate (Mgco3) was found in it. He filed a criminal complaint before the learned Jmfc for offence under Section 26(2) (1)/59 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The respondent No.1 then filed an application under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. stating that he is not the manufacturer of the Food Article Pan Parag. He claimed to be only the shopkeeper and alleging that the manufacturer and packing was done by the present petitioners. He requested the Court to implead the company Pan Parag and its manufacturer, as accused in the case. The learned Jmfc after affording opportunity to the prosecution passed the order stating that evidence has not been recorded in the case in hand. , therefore, application under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. is not maintainable. The accused/respondent No.1 filed criminal revision No.91/2015, learned Second Asj, Sagar vide order dated 27/08/2015 has held that the manufacturer of Pan Parag Pan Masala is a company and by virtue of Section 66 of the Food Standard and Safety Act, 2006 and is Managing Director may be prosecuted. He referred the case of Dharam Pal & others Vs. State of Haryana & another reported as (2014) 3 Scc 306. Anand Vikram Singh Bhadoriya vs Virendra Kumar Jain on 6 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35903248/ 1 The authorized representative of the company Pan Parag India Ltd. and the Managing Director of Pan Parag Ltd. have moved this revision in this background, it is claimed that the learned Revisional Court erred in passing the order impugned. The decision rendered by Honble Supreme Court in Dharam Pal (supra) has been misconstrued. It is further claimed that no prima facie case is made out against the petitioner. Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that in the case of Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab reported as Air 2014 Sc 1400, it has been made clear that the power under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. can only be exercised on the basis of fresh evidence brought before the Court. It is further claimed that the learned Revisional Court passed the order impugned erroneously. The application under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. during the course of enquiry remains limited to the extend that adding a person as an accused whose name has been mentioned in column No.2 of the charge-sheet or any other person who might be accomplished. Per contra, learned Panel Lawyer for respondent/State vehemently opposed the contentions and submit that the learned Revisional Court has analyzed the legal aspects and allowed the revision which is not called for any interference. Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 also submits that the order of the Revisional Court case (supra) in which it has been held that even without recording evidence, upon committal under Section 209 of Cr.P.C., the Session Judge may summon those persons shown in Column No.2 of For all offences, the Court of Magistrate is competent to arraign person as an accused from and during stage of cognizance itself under Section 190 of Cr.P.C. Following the law laid down in Dharam Pal's case (supra), the learned Revisional Court has passed the order.
